findings.evidence: "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter."
findings.fix: Consolidate into one Overview section and clarify which team publishes the log and whether it's quarterly or after open enrollment.
findings.violation: Contradicts the second Overview section, which states "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Delete this sentence entirely, or replace it with general policy language about backup reviewers and approval routing.
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph
findings.violation: This describes an operational problem or incident rather than stating policy; it should not appear in a formal policy document.

findings.evidence: "The request is reviewed within two business days."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the two-business-day timeline applies only to complete requests with both reviewers available, or revise both sections for consistency.
findings.violation: Contradicts the preceding "How to Apply" section, which states "the review takes longer" due to manager absence.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Rewrite as either "The manager approves items using the standard review checklist" or "The manager approves items with discretion within the standard review categories" to clarify the relationship.
findings.violation: Unclear whether the manager can override the checklist or must follow it; "notwithstanding" suggests discretion overrides the checklist, but this conflicts with the reference to the checklist itself.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first paragraph
findings.violation: Switches inconsistently from "you" to "we"; the document should use consistent voice throughout.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Define what "stipend item" means (the purchased equipment or the reimbursement amount), or remove this section and move process steps to the appropriate section.
findings.violation: This section uses "stipend item" three times without defining it, and includes process steps that belong in "How to Apply," not terminology definitions.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: List all required steps in the order they appear in the portal, or expand the description to match what the portal actually requires.
findings.violation: Lists only two steps but the policy states "The portal walks through each step in order," implying more steps exist.

findings.evidence: Two separate section headings titled "## Overview" (one as "## Program Overview" and another as "## Overview")
findings.fix: Merge the two sections into one "Program Overview" or consolidate the information and use distinct section titles for each.
findings.violation: Having two overview-type sections creates structural confusion and makes the document harder to navigate.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the vendor list each quarter."
findings.fix: Retitle the section "Vendor List and Audit Records" or move this content to a more appropriate section, and rewrite to address how employees get answers to questions.
findings.violation: This sentence starts the "Questions and Updates" section but addresses vendor list maintenance, not customer questions or update mechanisms.
